world_prompt.text_prompt: The scene is an extremely photorealistic, fully explorable 3D reconstruction of the historic Old Town of Prague, Czech Republic, as it exists in the real world today, captured through high-quality real-world photography or 3D scanning. The overall tone is calm and authentic, reflecting the natural beauty of a historic European city at dusk. The environment meticulously recreates the atmosphere of the narrow historic streets around Prague's Old Town Square, featuring authentic Czech architecture, including Gothic and Baroque buildings, Renaissance facades, and natural pastel-colored plaster walls. Traditional tiled rooftops crown the structures, while historic stone buildings line the realistic cobblestone streets. Buildings exhibit believable architectural structures with correct window proportions, realistic entrances, stone foundations, wooden doors, and detailed roof edges. Subtle signs of natural aging are evident, such as weathered plaster, slight discoloration, and worn stone surfaces, all contributing to realistic material variations without excessive decay. Realistic historic street lamps, authentic shop signs with realistic thickness and mounting structures, metal brackets, detailed window frames with glass panes, rain gutters, door handles, hinges, and flower boxes are all physically integrated into their surroundings. Street lamps feature detailed metal frames and glass surfaces, realistically connected to nearby buildings. Windows possess accurate depth, realistic glass transparency, and reflections corresponding to the surrounding street. The scene is set during a calm, clear early evening, shortly after sunset, with realistic ambient daylight and a slightly cool sky, combined with subtle warm illumination from actual street lamps and a few building windows. Consistent lighting direction, natural shadow transitions, realistic light falloff, and believable reflections on glass, metal, and stone are meticulously rendered. Physically plausible materials are used for stone, plaster, wood, glass, and metal, avoiding excessively glossy surfaces or artificial saturation.
